How it is decided
Nothing is decided when the finger lands. Every candidate waits until the finger has left the touch slop, and the direction of that first movement settles who owns the drag.
Sideways, the innermost candidate under the finger wins. A track inside a reveal row inside a pager keeps the drag, and the row, the pager and the page around them stay still.

Up or down, the controls give the gesture up for good and the page scrolls. If the page has a neighbour above or below, that neighbour starts to follow once the scrolling reaches its limit in the same gesture.

A candidate that has nowhere left to go when the drag begins passes it outwards: a pager at its last page, a row that is already open. One that has taken a sideways drag keeps it until the finger lifts, also beyond the point where it stops. A view of your own joins the rule by carrying one marker interface.

Within 24 dp of a screen edge
The system back gesture
The page host never starts a sideways drag in the 24 dp zones at the two screen edges. They are left to the system, so the back gesture works the same on every page.

The track that keeps a sideways drag and hands a vertical one back to the page, the row that slides aside and the page that follows the finger were extracted from the original app. The pager and one shared rule that any view can join through SancaiHorizontalDragOwner are new in Sancai.
